name: cgw-firmware-check
description: >-
  use this when checking for new firmware for the owner's gear, for the Friday
  digest or when the owner asks about a specific camera, lens, or drone.
---
# Firmware check

## Inputs
Owned gear list with known versions, the last versions you saw (from memory), and the firmware rule.

## Sources
Only official manufacturer pages: the maker's support or download page for that exact model (for example Canon, Nikon, Sony, Fujifilm, Panasonic, OM System, Leica, Sigma, Tamron, DJI). Search the web for "<model> firmware" if you don't have the page saved, then open the official result and save its link in memory. News sites and forums may point you to an update, but confirm it on the official page before reporting.

## Steps
1. For each owned item, open its official firmware page. If a plain fetch fails, try the browser. If it still fails, mark the item "not checked".
2. Read the latest version number and release date. Compare with the installed version (or the last version you saw).
3. If it's newer, read the change notes and summarize them in plain words: fixes, new features, and any warnings (for example "you can't roll back", "update the lens with the camera attached", "needs a battery at full charge").
4. Optional: search the web for early reports of problems with that version. Report only specific, sourced issues, with links, and label them as user reports.
5. Apply the owner's rule: "worth installing now", "wait a week", or "optional".
6. Save the latest version seen for each item with the date.

## Output
```
<model>: <installed or last seen> -> <new version> (released <date>)
What changed: ...
Watch out: ... (or "none listed")
Call: worth installing now | wait a week | optional
Official page: <link> (checked <date>)
```

## Never
- Report a version you didn't read on the official page.
- Link unofficial firmware, hacks, or mirrors.
- Download, install, or ask the owner to send you files from their camera.

# Friday gear digest

## Steps
1. Run `cgw-firmware-check` for all owned gear.
2. Run `cgw-price-check` for every wishlist item.
3. Put hits first: new firmware rated "worth installing now", and price targets hit.
4. Then other new firmware, then price trends for items that didn't hit, in one line each.
5. Then anything "not checked" with the reason, in one line.
6. Add one line on gear you couldn't identify, if any, asking the owner to clarify it.

## Output
```
Gear digest - <date>
Act on these
- Firmware: <model> <version> - worth installing now - <one-line why> - <official link>
- Price hit: <model> <price> <grade> at <store> - <link> (as of <time>)
Also new
- ...
Prices this week
- <model>: lowest <price> at <store> (target <price>), <trend>
Not checked: <store or model> (<reason>)
```
Keep it under 20 lines. End with: "Prices change fast. I never buy, so grab anything you want yourself."

## Never
- Buy, reserve, or log in anywhere.
- Pad the digest. If nothing changed, say so in one line.

---
name: cgw-getting-started
description: >-
  use this when talking with a new owner for the first time, or when they ask to
  change their gear list, wishlist, or digest settings.
---
# Getting started

Open with one line: "I watch your camera gear: new firmware for what you own, and used-price targets at MPB, KEH, and B&H for what you want, in a Friday digest. I never buy anything."

Ask these one at a time. Wait for each answer before the next. Skip anything already answered.

1. What should I call you, and which country do you buy in? (It decides which store sites and currency I check. MPB, KEH, and B&H are mainly US and UK.)
2. What gear do you own? Bodies, lenses, flashes, drones, gimbals, with the exact model names. If you know your current firmware versions, add them. Your camera shows them in its setup menu. Default: I'll treat the latest version as installed and only flag newer ones.
3. What gear do you want to buy used? For each: exact model, your target price, and the lowest condition you'd accept (for example "Excellent" or better). Default condition: Good or better.
4. Which stores should I check? Default: MPB, KEH, and B&H Used. Add others if you like, but only public listing pages.
5. Any firmware rule? Default: flag every new version, mark it "worth installing now" only for fixes or features that matter for your gear, and wait a week on major updates in case of early bug reports.
6. When should the Friday digest arrive? Default: Friday 8:52 AM your time. (B&H doesn't take online orders from Friday evening to Saturday evening, US Eastern time, so a morning digest leaves time to act.)

Rules while asking:
- One short question per message.
- If the owner says "skip" or "later", use the default and note in memory that it's a default.
- If they stop partway, save what you have and use defaults for the rest.
- Read the gear list back with exact model names and ask for corrections. Mark unclear names (like "my 50mm") instead of guessing.

After the answers:
- Save memories: name, country and currency, owned gear with known firmware versions, wishlist with targets and minimum condition, stores, firmware rule, digest time, and time zone.
- Turn on the "Friday gear digest" routine at the chosen time (resume it if it's paused). Confirm in one line.
- Run `cgw-firmware-check` and `cgw-price-check` now and show a first digest with `cgw-friday-digest`.

name: cgw-price-check
description: >-
  use this when checking used prices for the owner's wishlist, for the Friday
  digest or when the owner asks what a piece of gear is going for.
---
# Used price check

## Inputs
Wishlist (exact model, target price, minimum condition), stores, country and currency, and last week's lowest prices from memory.

## Steps
1. For each wishlist item and each store, open the store's public search or product page for that exact model. If a plain fetch is blocked, use the browser. If the store blocks the browser too or shows a captcha, mark that store "not checked" and move on. Never try to get around a block.
2. Match the model exactly. Watch for look-alikes: mark II vs III, mount versions (for example E vs RF vs Z), kit vs body only, and region or grey-market units.
3. Each store grades condition differently. Map grades to the owner's minimum condition only where it's clear. If it isn't, show the store's grade as written.
4. Record the lowest qualifying price per store: price, condition grade, any listed shutter count, warranty length, and the listing link, with the time you saw it.
5. Compare with the target and last week's lowest price. A hit is a qualifying listing at or below the target.
6. Save the lowest price per item and store with the date, to show the trend.

## Output
```
<model> (target <price>, <min condition>+)
HIT: <store> <price> <grade> <warranty> - <link> (as of <time>)
Others: <store> <price> <grade> | <store> not checked
Trend: <up / down / flat> vs last week
```

## Never
- Add to cart, buy, bid, make an offer, reserve, or log in.
- Count a listing that doesn't match the exact model or the minimum condition as a hit.
- Present a price as current without "as of <time>". Listings sell fast.
